# Chatbot Requirements Quality Checklist: Taskify Company Knowledge Q&A

**Purpose**: Review requirement completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability for private company-knowledge chat before task generation.
**Created**: 2026-10-20
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Depth**: Standard
**Audience / Timing**: Reviewer; specification and design review before `$speckit-tasks`.
**Focus**: Company/account privacy and access; grounded conversational answers and refusal boundaries, including the requested model-configuration contract.

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are company-isolation requirements defined for knowledge, factual answers, source metadata, and resource existence information? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK002 Are private conversation ownership requirements explicit for users, same-company admins, and accounts in other companies? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, Spec §SC-011]
- [ ] CHK003 Are account provisioning, the two roles, first-party login, and the boundary between operator and company-admin authority fully specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–FR-006, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK004 Are evidence and source-link requirements defined for every factual answer, including follow-ups and conflicting company sources? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012–FR-013, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements stated for each distinct response outcome: answer, refusal, insufficient information, clarification, and operational failure? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-021–FR-022]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is the boundary between an unrelated request and a company-related question without sufficient evidence defined using distinguishable criteria? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-021–FR-022]
- [ ] CHK007 Are permitted explanations of company information distinguished clearly from prohibited actions, independently of the orchestration choice? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, Spec §User Story 1, Plan §Chat workflow and persistence]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the required source-reference identity and location precise enough to distinguish the actual supporting resource from another revision or similarly named item? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011–FR-012, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK009 Are login-session expiry, saved conversation persistence, and bounded follow-up context described as distinct concepts? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-019–FR-020, Plan §Chat workflow and persistence]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the exact OPEN_AI_MODEL setting, required-value rules, absence of a hidden default, and separation from embedding configuration documented unambiguously? [Clarity, Plan §Chat model environment configuration]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Are company and private-chat access rules consistent across the specification, data ownership definitions, and interface requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-014, Spec §FR-019, Data Model §Ownership and common rules]
- [ ] CHK012 Are admin content-management permissions consistent with the requirement that chat cannot perform administrative actions, even for admins? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the meaning of source freshness consistent between the specification’s “before display” wording and the plan’s final response-release checkpoint? [Consistency, Conflict, Spec §FR-011, Spec §SC-007, Plan §Ingestion, embeddings, and source freshness]
- [ ] CHK014 Are model-selection requirements consistent for newly accepted requests and interrupted requests after a deployment configuration change? [Consistency, Plan §Chat model environment configuration, Data Model §Graph execution state and configuration]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Are “factually supported” and “unanswerable” defined with a review rubric, reference evidence, and representative evaluation-set selection criteria? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §SC-004, Spec §SC-009, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK016 Are the case boundaries and pass criteria for privacy, refusal, and mixed-request acceptance outcomes objectively stated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, Spec §SC-010–SC-011]
- [ ] CHK017 Are response-time targets defined with a clear start/end point, percentile, concurrency conditions, and distinction from the maximum processing deadline? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, Plan §Performance Goals, Plan §Chat workflow and persistence]
- [ ] CHK018 Are file-readiness targets tied to a defined representative corpus, supported formats, processing-time boundary, and treatment of failed items? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006, Spec §Assumptions]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are primary requirements complete for initial access, a first company question, and resumption of the same private conversation after reauthentication? [Coverage, Primary Flow, Spec §User Story 1, Spec §User Story 2, Spec §SC-012]
- [ ] CHK020 Are alternate-flow requirements defined for contextual follow-ups, ambiguous references, conflicting evidence, and references outside the available conversational context? [Coverage, Alternate Flow, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-020, Plan §Chat workflow and persistence]
- [ ] CHK021 Are exception requirements defined separately for unavailable dependencies, invalid answer evidence, insufficient company information, and an expired login during an answer? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-022, Plan §Chat workflow and persistence]
- [ ] CHK022 Are recovery requirements explicit for interrupted answers, repeated submissions, deliberate retries, and preservation of the saved conversation without duplicate responses? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Spec §FR-019, Plan §Chat workflow and persistence]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 Are mixed requests and attempts to override the company-only rules through questions, earlier messages, or company documents explicitly addressed? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-020–FR-022, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Are concurrent knowledge replacement/removal and historical source unavailability covered without silently changing the evidence associated with an earlier answer? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-010–FR-011, Spec §SC-007, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements specified for multiple initial-password sessions, password-change invalidation, and pending answers when authentication changes? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-005–FR-006, Plan §Authentication and validation]
- [ ] CHK026 Are boundary-input requirements complete for blank or oversized questions, malformed identifiers, duplicate identities, and unsupported, corrupt, empty, or unreadable files? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-015–FR-017, Spec §SC-008]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK027 Are privacy requirements documented for information sent to the AI provider, retained conversations, secrets, operational records, and access to company resources? [Completeness, Security, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-014, Spec §FR-019, Research §R-09]
- [ ] CHK028 Are accessibility and asynchronous-feedback requirements stated for the chat, source references, authentication errors, and processing outcomes? [Completeness, Accessibility, Frontend Contract §Chat interaction, Frontend Contract §Accessibility and verification]
- [ ] CHK029 Are capacity, overload, dependency-unavailability, and recovery expectations quantified or explicitly identified as deferred requirements? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §SC-005–SC-006, Plan §Scale/Scope, Plan §Delivery and verification sequence]
- [ ] CHK030 Are ownership, validation, compatibility, and complete documentation obligations stated for every affected feature boundary? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, Constitution §Core Principles, Plan §Constitution Check]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK031 Are requirements for provider/model compatibility, unavailable model selections, and configuration changes documented without assuming all models have equivalent capabilities? [Dependency, Plan §Chat model environment configuration, Research §R-10]
- [ ] CHK032 Are the supported document/image content, readable-text expectations, language assumptions, and intentionally unsupported formats explicitly bounded? [Assumption, Spec §FR-007–FR-008, Spec §Assumptions, Research §R-05]
- [ ] CHK033 Are operator provisioning access and trusted initial-credential distribution documented as dependencies, with responsibility for each assigned? [Dependency, Assumption, Spec §FR-003–FR-005, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK034 Are retention, deletion, and bounded conversational context distinguished, with unresolved policy choices explicitly identified rather than implied by persistent history? [Ambiguity, Gap, Spec §FR-019–FR-020, Spec §Assumptions, Data Model §Validation and consistency matrix]
- [ ] CHK035 Are additional content-processing limits distinguished from published input limits, with their effect on accepted-file guarantees stated explicitly? [Conflict, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-016, Spec §SC-008, Research §R-05]
- [ ] CHK036 Is the deferral of account recovery and deactivation accompanied by explicit assumptions for lost credentials and users who must lose company access? [Gap, Assumption, Spec §FR-005–FR-006, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- All generated items are intentionally unchecked; generation does not evaluate or approve the requirements.
- A Gap, Ambiguity, or Conflict tag identifies a review question, not an adjudicated finding.
- Assess the wording and coverage of requirements, rather than application behavior or implementation completion.
- Scope and standard depth are inferred from the active feature and recent clarifications; no narrower focus was supplied.
- Latest must-haves are represented: one private saved conversation per account, linked company evidence, refusal of unrelated requests and actions, and the exact OPEN_AI_MODEL runtime setting. Orchestration choices remain supporting design context rather than implementation checks.
- Source references use real requirement IDs or document section names. Supporting documents: [plan](../plan.md), [research](../research.md), [data model](../data-model.md), [internal contracts](../contracts/internal.md), [frontend contract](../contracts/frontend.md), and [constitution](../../../.specify/memory/constitution.md).
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied. Leave unresolved items unchecked and record findings inline.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`; this custom checklist does not change it.
